steps.text: Preheat oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Melt butter in a 9 x 9 inch baking dish.
Blend together flour, baking powder, sugar, and milk.
Pour batter in baking dish over the butter. Sprinkle fruit on top of the batter, do not stir. Bake for 1 hour or until golden brown.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Fruit Cobbler
raw_recipe.description: For this delicious, simple pie, all you 'll need is a 9x9-inch pan, melted butter, a yummy batter and some sliced, fresh fruit. The batter goes in the pan, the fruit is poured on top of the batter, and the cobbler is baked in the oven for an hour.
raw_recipe.name: Easy Fruit Cobbler

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Melt butter in a 9 x 9 inch baking dish.
Blend together flour, baking powder, sugar, and milk.
Pour batter in baking dish over the butter. Sprinkle fruit on top of the batter, do not stir. Bake for 1 hour or until golden brown.

review.reviewBody:
This fast, easy, and delicious. I did do somethings differently. First I added about 
1 tsp of vanilla extract to the batter mix. Secondly, I baked the batter for about ten minutes before adding the fruit (I used red delicious apples, turned out fine) Lastly, I sprinkled brown sugar on top, giving it a nice brown color after it baked. My family just loved it!

yummy, but I changed it up a bit as well. Used 1 c. buttermilk, 1/2 c white sugar, 3/4 c whole wheat flour, 1/4 c unbleached, 1/4 c rolled oats, 2 t baking powder, pinch of salt. Mixed 2-3 T of soft butter right into the batter, added a little of the LIGHT syrup from the canned peaches to smooth it out. Sprayed non-stick spray in 8x8 pan. Sprinkled Cinnamon on the chopped canned peaches, poured batter on top.

The only change I made was I doubled it and baked it in a 9×13 glass pan. It required longer baking time, so I just checked it every 5-7 minutes until my chop stick came out clean. I used 2 cans of peaches for the fruit. It turned out just like the fruit cobbler from my childhood, and the family enjoyed it, too.

One thing that will help sweeten the cobbler if making with variety of berries is to macerate the fruit first--put in bowl--sprinkle about 2 Tablsp. sugar over top of berries--then because I'm more tactile than daughter--I reach in with CLEAN hands and kind of mash or squish a few (not all) of the berries up--she presses a glass down to crush a few berries and get the juices flowing--let that sit while oven preheating and toss together the rest of recipe. Made it twice and first time I left rack in middle of oven and turned out a tad gooey in center--second time I place oven rack up a notch and turned out evenly baked throughout--good recipe for if you're in a hurry.
Been using this recipe since my stepfather told me about it 3-4 decades ago. Most recently tried it w/canned pineapples! Brown sugar goes on the bottom of the pan (along w/butter). My new fave!

Made it by using canned cherries and adding a touch of vanilla to the batter. I mixed all ingredients into the melted butter to save a bowl, and also sprinkled a bit of sugar on top. Yum. Reminds me of Mom’s cherry cobbler.

Very easy and very fast!!! I used cherry pie filling so I think that I should use less sugar next time. I also add 1 tsp of vanilla in the mix. The butter at the bottom made tha dough crunchy and delicious.Also, I made it in my airfrier/multi... new French doors oven which is a challenge because temperature and timing is different from conv. ovens. Did it in a Pirex for 20 min. And covered with foil about 10-15 min more. Same temp. 325°F.Perfect!!!I don't understand why some people rate you with 1 or 2 stars... I would say that they must be really bad cooks.I am eating it right now and I could say that is amazingly good!!!
After reading reviews we added 1tsp vanilla and baked for 10 minutes before adding fruit. Also only used 1 cup of chopped fresh strawberries mixed with 1 - 2 tsp sugar. Very easy and very good.

I did a 1.5 recipe so it'd fit in a 13x9 pan. I used 2c of strawberries and 1c blackberries. Made as directed except I sprinkled a little sugar on the berries since they were fresh. It came out beautifully and was festive for the 4th of July! It was quick and easy too.

Sometimes you just need something fast. I made it twice, once with canned peaches and once with frozen berries. Also, I used Splenda, instead of sugar. Cooked about 6 minutes longer with the berries to assure the batter was completely done. Great with ice cream or with whipped cream.

My mother, Lila, used to make peach cobblers with a similar/same recipe. I used your delightful recipe with Sugar in the Raw, baked the pastry for 10 minutes before adding the peaches on top, liberally seasoned the peaches with cinnamon, drizzled 1 tablespoon of butter over the entire dish about 10 minutes before the end of the one hour baking time. I also used a glass casserole dish, as my mother used to use a beat-up deep cobbler tin pot. It was yummy-delicious-goodness-oh-my-gawwwwwd good, just like my mother's, every time. Thanks for sharing all the tips in the comments, fellow bakers and kitchen adventurers.
My grandmother taught me to make this with Bisquick when I was still in elementary school. She took it to church quite often.
Too cakey. Needs less breading and more buttery crispiness and sugary gooey berries. Not a recipe I’ll use again.

I have been making this recipe for years and everyone loves it. I have been asked many times to write it down for them!! Sometimes I add a sprinkle of cinnamon before baking. It is good either way. Enjoy!!!!
The best recipe for any fruit - fresh or frozen!
I added a 1/4 tsp of nutmeg to the batter.

This is an old school Southern recipe. I use Bisquick therefore no need for baking powder. I have made it with blackberries a number of times. Great with mixed berries also. Georgia peaches is a favorite also. I sprinkle a little more sugar on top before baking!!!

Double recipe (or use half pan), my family loved it so much! I thought it was a tad too sweet, but they didn't. Added some cinnamon and vanilla to the fruits. I love that I can use any fruit, used some frozen fruit the kids poo poo for smoothies, but devoured in the cobbler.
Fabulous with peaches and also blueberries!!
